title: ContractingProcess
description: One complete procurement, from planning through tender, award, and contract - the spine that OCDS calls a contracting process, identified by an ocid. Everything that happens hangs off this one identifier, which is what makes it possible to follow a single purchase from the budget line that funded it to the supplier that was paid. schema.org has no tender, procurement, bid, or solicitation concept; Demand and Offer are retail constructs carrying GTIN, SKU and warranty semantics that do not apply, so nothing is gained by forcing a tender into them.

ocid.description: Open Contracting ID: a globally unique identifier for this process, prefixed with a registered publisher prefix. The join key across publishers and the reason OCDS data is aggregatable at all.

buyer.description: The GovernmentOrganization paying. Required: a procurement with no accountable buyer cannot be audited.

budgetLine.description: The BudgetLine(s) funding this process. The join to the budget profile, and the link that answers 'what did we actually buy with that appropriation'.

party.description: References to the non-government Party entities involved. Government participants are reached through buyer and tender.procuringEntity instead, so a body is never duplicated as both an organization and a party.
